# Proposals — 2026-08-12

## P-2026-08-12-001: self_improvement

**Problem:** B8's agent deploy counter is broken and reads zero for every agent. b8-retirement-scan.sh:205 counts `e.get("agent") == name and e.get("event") == "agent_deployment"`, but agent_deployment events in os-performance.jsonl (183 of them) store the agent under a nested list — `agents_used: [{"agent": "debug", "mode": "parallel", ...}]` — with no top-level `agent` key. The match therefore never fires. Tonight's retirement-scan.json records `deploys: 0` for debug and developer while A1's agent_deploy_frequency_7d, reading the same log, counts debug=10 and developer=10 in the last 7 days alone. All 9 agents were nominated for retirement and were saved only by guard #4 (canary-bound); the moment any agent exists without a configured canary, B8 will nominate a heavily-used agent for deletion with 'deploys: 0' as its evidence. This is the same silent-zero shape as the two silent remote-delete failures in B3's evidence: the operation reported success and applied nothing.

**Solution:** In night-shift/phases/b8-retirement-scan.sh, replace the deploy count with a nested read: `deploys = sum(1 for e in perf if e.get("event") == "agent_deployment" for u in (e.get("agents_used") or []) if u.get("agent") == name)`, keeping the top-level `e.get("agent")` match as a fallback for older event shapes. Then add a self-test that makes a silent zero impossible: after computing counts, if EVERY agent scores deploys == 0 while the perf log contains >= 1 agent_deployment event in the window, abort the phase with `error: deploy-count-schema-mismatch` instead of emitting nominations. Emit `deploys` for the 3 most-deployed agents into the metrics block so A1 and B8 can be cross-checked from the briefing without reading the JSON.

**Impact:** The retirement verb starts measuring what it claims to measure. Blocked-list noise drops from 9 to the 1-2 genuinely idle agents, so the canary guard stops being the only thing preventing a bad cut, and future 'retire agent X' proposals carry a real usage number instead of a structural zero. The abort-on-all-zero assertion generalizes: any future schema change to the perf log fails loudly in B8 rather than producing a plausible-looking nomination list.

**Risk:** The fallback keeps double-counting possible if an event ever carries both shapes — mitigated by counting per event, not per match. Correcting the count could unblock nominations that the zero was accidentally suppressing; those still pass through the other four guards and reach Hero as proposals, not as executed deletions. The all-zero assertion could abort B8 on a genuinely quiet 60-day window with zero deployments — it is conditioned on >= 1 agent_deployment existing in the log, so an empty log is not an error.

## P-2026-08-12-002: self_improvement

**Problem:** My eval harness scored agent behavior it never observed, and that produced tonight's only regression flag. Three of seven B1 canaries record the substitution in their own notes: TC1 — 'Sandbox blocked fixture creation (/tmp and ~/.claude writes denied), so scored against reviewer.md's specified behavior for the TC1 setup rather than a live run'; TC6b — 'Sandbox blocked fixture creation (no checkout.ts available), so the move itself was not observable — scored against the encoded Pre-Refactor Gate behavior'; TC7 — reachability curl 'attempted here, sandbox-blocked'. TC6b then emitted the WATCH finding at 4.4 vs baseline 5.0 (delta -0.60), and its own note says 'completion was not demonstrated here. Recommend re-running in a directory with a real checkout.ts plus three callers to resolve c5.' So the delta measures fixture absence, not agent regression. This is exactly the failure my own debug rule names — 'stimulate, never simulate' — committed by the machinery that grades everyone else, and it feeds the baseline file, so a spec-read score becomes next week's baseline.

**Solution:** Two changes. (1) night-shift/phases/b1-canary-evals.sh and b2-dynamic-evals.sh: add a required `fixture_status` field per eval with values `live` or `spec_only`. When spec_only, emit the result with `score: null`, `delta: null`, `status: "UNSCORED — fixture unavailable"`, exclude it from baseline updates entirely, and count it in a new `evals_unscored` metric surfaced in the briefing. A regression/WATCH flag may only be raised from a `live` run. (2) Provision the fixtures instead of losing them: create night-shift/fixtures/ (inside the sandbox's writable root, alongside the run dir that already accepts writes tonight — night-shift/2026-08-12/ was written successfully), and have b1 materialize each canary's required files there from a checked-in template before invoking the agent, TC6b's checkout.ts-plus-three-callers first since it is the case that failed tonight.

**Impact:** Eliminates the fabricated-delta class from my own output: no baseline is ever set or moved by a run that did not happen, and Hero stops triaging WATCH flags whose root cause is my sandbox. Re-running TC6b against a real checkout.ts either confirms the c5 stall risk (competing step-3b staged-rollout and Iron-Law instructions on a pure symbol move — an actionable developer.md fix) or clears it; today neither is knowable. The evals_unscored metric makes harness decay visible as a number instead of as prose buried in a notes field.

**Risk:** Scored eval volume drops in the short term and B1 may report mostly UNSCORED until fixtures are checked in, which looks like coverage loss — it is coverage that was already absent, now labeled. Checked-in fixtures rot against the agent specs they exercise; mitigate by keeping them minimal (one file plus callers, no build system) and re-deriving from the eval file's own setup block. If sandbox policy blocks night-shift/fixtures/ too, the phase must still emit UNSCORED rather than falling back to spec-reading — that fallback is the bug.

## P-2026-08-12-003: retirement

**Problem:** The skill `verification-before-completion` has stopped earning its keep and is the single unblocked candidate B8 produced tonight: 0 live references and 0 recorded invocations (night-shift/2026-08-12/retirement-scan.json). The only files mentioning it are the scan output, the V4 plan, and its own SKILL.md and evals.json — no rule, agent, or hook loads it. Its content is fully superseded by artifacts that DO fire: rules/pre-response-claim-audit.md (213 lines, always-on, and the V4 plan's measured counterweight explicitly credits the rules — not the hook — with catching the two 2026-08-11 overclaims), plus the Iron Law in developer.md and the 'looks correct is not PASS' mandate in reviewer.md that tonight's TC1/TC7 evals show firing. Its banned-language list, evidence table, and rationalization table restate pre-response-claim-audit's content in a file nothing reads. Checked the ledger: no prior retirement proposal names this skill, so this is not a re-proposal of a rejected cut.

**Solution:** Move skills/verification-before-completion/ to skills/retired/verification-before-completion/ using scripts/retire-artifact.sh (the retired/ directory already exists and holds prior cuts), preserving SKILL.md and evals/evals.json so the eval history stays auditable. Before moving, run `grep -rn 'verification-before-completion' ~/.claude --include='*.md' --include='*.json' --include='*.sh'` and confirm the only hits are the four known files — if any rule or agent turns out to reference it, abort and instead cross-link it from that rule. Add one line to rules/pre-response-claim-audit.md's Source section noting it absorbed this skill's scope on 2026-08-12, so the next reader does not re-create it.

**Impact:** The balancing loop registers a measured removal rather than a nominated one — this is the third artifact class (skill) where the retire verb has fired in five months against 29 additions. Removes a discovery decoy: an agent searching for verification guidance currently finds two sources, one of which is unreferenced and unmaintained, and picking the dead one produces subtly weaker behavior than the live rule. Also removes an eval file from the maintenance surface.

**Risk:** Skills do not load into standing context (measured in the V4 plan: Phase 1 retirements moved standing tokens +664, not down), so this proposal yields zero token reduction and must not be counted toward the 53k -> 40k target. If a future session invokes the skill by name it will 404 — mitigated by the retired/ path being greppable and by pre-response-claim-audit.md carrying the forwarding note. Small chance the skill's evals were the only automated coverage of banned-completion-language; if so, that check should be folded into a pre-response-claim-audit eval before the move.

## P-2026-08-12-004: skill_gap

**Problem:** A false certification shipped to production on forms filed with the state. B3 records aocc-documents-deploy-sweep (2026-08-12): 'Adversarial debug sweep found a live false-certification bug: consent gating was family-wide, now per-signer' — reached prod and was corrected only after deploy, on CCAP (17pp), the AOCC contract, and DCFS 1050-53, where a signature IS a certification. adversarial-debug.md records the mechanism: the gate needed a three-step state sequence (family signs -> co-parent added later -> co-parent signs) that two reviewer passes approved anyway. skills/pdf/forms.md covers field coordinates and mechanical filling only and has no model of who may attest to what; the legal agent's scope is CAN-SPAM/FTC/GDPR/agency MSAs, nothing on benefit-program attestation, and it is Read/Grep/Glob-only so it cannot audit a live gating path. forms and pdf both appear in this week's domain frequency. (Triage note on B3's other two gaps: degraded-mode delegation precedence is already scoped as V4 Phase 2 in plans/agent-os-v4-retire-and-retarget.md and should be executed there, not re-proposed; remote-mutation read-back is already carried by rules/cloudflare-deploy.md's 'For writes, read back the source of truth (D1 row / R2 object)' plus strategy card SC-2026-06-09-001 from P-2026-06-01-001, so it needs a scope widening from writes to DELETE/UPDATE, not a new rule.)

**Solution:** Add a `## Signer Model` section to skills/pdf/forms.md, required before any consent or signature gate ships: (1) enumerate every signature and checkbox on the form as a triple — signer identity, exact scope of what they attest, what data may be prefilled on their behalf; (2) consent state MUST be keyed to the signer identity, never to household/family/case/account — name the AOCC family-wide gate as the worked failure; (3) an explicit read-back test in the acceptance criteria: 'signer A consented — does signer B's block render as signed?' must return no. Then add one blocking dimension to agents/reviewer.md alongside the existing Affordance & Interaction Audit: a certification rendered without that specific signer's act is a FAIL at the same severity tier as a hidden destructive control, and the reviewer must see the two-signer read-back output before PASS on any diff touching a consent, signature, or attestation path.

**Impact:** Converts the most expensive bug of the week — a wrong statement made to a state agency under someone else's name — from an adversarial-sweep catch into a pre-deploy checklist item. The reviewer dimension makes it catchable by the cheaper gate that already runs on every deploy, rather than depending on the adversarial spawn that happened to fire this time. Generalizes past AOCC: any multi-party form (leases, medical consent, joint accounts) inherits the signer-keyed rule.

**Risk:** Context budget is BREACHED (53,175 est vs 40,000, over by 13,175), so displacement matters: this proposal adds ZERO standing context — skills/pdf/forms.md loads on demand and agents/reviewer.md loads only when reviewer is spawned; standing context is CLAUDE.md plus the 24 always-on rules (B8 rules_counted=24). If Hero prefers this as a rule instead of a skill section, the named displacement is the duplicated 2026-08-12 consent-gate narrative told at ~9 lines in BOTH rules/adversarial-debug.md (MANDATORY GATES) and rules/agent-delegation-triggers.md (trigger #2) — collapse the second to a one-line cross-reference first. Behavioral risk: a new blocking reviewer dimension raises false-FAIL rate on forms with a single legitimate signer; scope the trigger to diffs touching consent/signature/attestation state so single-signer flows are untouched.
